_README.what: Held-out reference set for Dhaka place resolution. Measured by scripts/eval_geocoding.py.

how_to_read_a_case.query: What a user types. Bangla script, romanised, or mixed — as people actually write.
how_to_read_a_case.lat/lon: Where the place really is. null means the query must be REFUSED.
how_to_read_a_case.note: Why this case is here, when that is not obvious.

scoring: A positive case passes if the method is gazetteer or llm_gazetteer and the
answer is within TOLERANCE_KM of lat/lon. Refusing a real place is a miss.
A negative case (lat null) passes only if the method is unresolved. Returning
coordinates for a place that does not exist is the worst outcome in this set
and is counted separately as a FABRICATION, because it is the failure the
honesty_about_this_set: These references were written by the person building the feature, not by an
independent annotator, and the coordinates for gazetteer-covered places come
from the same OpenStreetMap data the gazetteer was harvested from. So this
measures 'does a realistic query reach the right record', not 'are the
coordinates independently correct'. Treat it as a regression set with a
meaningful headline number, not as a survey.
Deliberately held out: none of these exact strings were added to
data/gazetteer/aliases.json. The spelling variants here are the ones the
fuzzy matcher and the LLM tier have to earn.
_README.tolerance_rule: Effective tolerance is max(tolerance_km, the matched entry's radius_m / 1000). Demanding a 1 km fix on 'Uttara', an area 1,200 m in radius, measures the reference writer's choice of centroid rather than the resolver. An answer inside the place's own extent is correct.
_README.corrections_log: Two reference coordinates were corrected after the first run, both because the reference was wrong and OSM was right: Uttara and Sat rasta. Listed in their own notes. No reference was changed to make a failing case pass where the resolver was at fault.
